Well If you like some kind of security challenges, you can play this game. As this is not hollywood movie style hacking game, where u are hacking NASA with html. Here actual unix commands are given to learn more about linux, networking security, ports and other cracking staffs. Recommended for those who kinda feel themselves "A Cyber Geek".

I will say that, for somebody who knows what they're doing, the hacking is a little on the easy side - however, that seems pretty reasonable for a game. I mean, you don't make a game exclusively for people who know how to navigate a linux file system - it just wouldn't sell enough.

With that said, I would never have believed that you could make me have so much fun typing commands into a shell prompt!

Whether you know anything about linux file systems or not you should give this game a try (the commands it uses are fairly limited and easy to pick up) - especially at this price. I spent most of my evening staring at text and I don't mind it at all. The music is fantastic and it has a fun story and a lot of fun easter eggs.

One con: I genuinely can't believe that, with all the work the developer put into this, that they have .exe's running on a linux machine - I just can't get over seeing ".exe" on every executable that you use in the game...

Still, it was a great training exercise in using the CLI. The moral grey areas of hacking are thought-provoking here. I just wish that it was playable. 

Maybe it's a compatibility issue with my Mac mini (2020). If PC owners are able to work around the glitches, then I definitely would recommend this game to them.

This is a really clever game that puts you in the role of a hacker who is investigating the death of another hacker.

The game will you have completing contracts and missions which involve connecting to other computers and trying to exploit their vulnerabilities using the tools and knowledge your given.

Whats great is that the game doesn't hold your hand too much so you have to figure out based on the knowledge and hacking scripts you have, how to complete your objective. Not everything can be solved by hacking either and you will need to gather info from files and to discover a hint about what to do next.

I'm far from an expert on hacking or cybersecurity but it does look like the game treats hacking in a more realistic way than what is usually shown in popular media i.e some person typing furiously on a keyboard while loads of green text flies across the screen.

Overall I really enjoyed Hacknet and would recommend it. It is at it's heart, a puzzle game and it is worth trying out if you fancy a puzzle game with unique approach.

Hacknet is a cool little immersive puzzler that does a great job of making you feel like a Hollywood hacker. It can also help you learn a few basic CLI/terminal commands, and possibly improve your typing skills--especially if you don't use all of the shortcuts. ;)

The stylized interface is mostly intuitive and functional, although the flash sometimes gets in the way--especially while running programs. The map is a condensed and cluttered version of the one in Uplink, but usually performs its job well enough. Discovered themes/layouts can be swapped at will, but something with true customization would have been a better option. The music and sound effects fit the atmosphere, and there are even a few fairly memorable tunes.

Some functions are weirdly prohibitive--like even the smallest note can take up most of the tiny amount of RAM on your static system. Executing and killing processes from the command line is usually much faster than trying to click on the animated visual elements. Your hardware cannot be altered or upgraded, and while you can explore and find tons of little secrets and easter eggs--including stashes of interesting data files or progs--there is very little sense of actual progression beyond the linear story missions. The integrated Mod support could help, but I have yet to try any of them, so I can't comment on their value.

There are bugs, and it is possible to actually break your game while messing with your in-game system (so that's more like a feature.) IMPORTANT: A long-standing bug can and will "corrupt" your save file if you use Cloud Saves. Disable that junk, unless you like the added challenge of fixing your save file with a text editor. I figured it out on my own by comparing saves from the GOG version that I played a few years ago, but if that doesn't sound fun, then kill cloud support.

Overall--it's a fun niche title with mystery, intrigue, humor, and secrets that allows you to play out a few vanilla hacker fantasies. Definitely worth playing if you're an Uplink fan or looking for something different.
